subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw land this focused async/yielding bootstrap implementation despite replacing Node fs.glob with a custom walker and changing hook scheduling on a session-sensitive hot path?
rationale: The patch is correct and well-proven for the reported stall, but automation cannot safely choose whether the remaining glob-parity, prompt-byte, and session-timing upgrade risks are acceptable.

options.title: Land After Exact-Head Checks
options.body: Accept the bounded internal compatibility risk and merge after the current head is validated against current main.

options.title: Require Connected Runtime Proof
options.body: Ask for one current-head embedded run with active channel or WebSocket traffic before accepting the scheduling change.

options.title: Pause For Broader Architecture
options.body: Keep or close the PR without merging if owners prefer worker isolation, priority scheduling, or caching over this focused mitigation.

recommendation.title: Land After Exact-Head Checks
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded internal compatibility risk and merge after the current head is validated against current main.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history spans all three decision surfaces: workspace reads, bootstrap hooks, and internal hook dispatch.
